newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Second Pakistani religious party boycotts polls.
newsitem.headline: Second Pakistani religious party boycotts polls.

text.p: Another Islamic religious party announced on Wednesday that it would boycott the Pakistani general election set for February 3.
Shah Ahmed Noorani said his Jamiat-e-Ulema-Pakistan party would not disrupt the vote but would not take part because its proposal for proportional representation had been ignored.
"The JUP has decided to stay away from the February 3 elections," he told a news conference.

The religious Jamaat-i-Islami party and the small Tehrik-e-Istiqlal party have already declared they will not participate in the poll, which is being organised by a caretaker government set up after President Farooq Leghari's dismissal of Benazir Bhutto as prime minister on November 5.

"We are not damaging democracy...we want to put democracy back on track by demanding accountability of corrupt politicians prior to the elections," Jamaat leader Qazi Hussain Ahmed told supporters at a protest sit-in in Karachi on Wednesday evening..
The Jamaat, which aims for an Islamic revolution, says it is boycotting the election because corrupt politicians are being allowed to take part.

Noorani said the JUP did not want the religious parties to be divided over the election issue, adding that the party would not demand that the voting be postponed. "We will not put up any resistance to the elections," he said.
Noorani said his party had scrutinised nomination papers and found that "feudal lords" and "looters of the national economy" were being allowed to participate.
The JUP had fielded candidates for 18 seats in the National Assembly (lower house) and 39 provincial assembly seats. Noorani said they had been told to withdraw their nominations.
